coding_note: Every non-numeric cell is backed by a verbatim quote with a locator. Cells without a supporting passage are coded not_stated and are never inferred. No inter-rater coefficient is reported; see rubric method note.

papers.label: LoCoMo
papers.title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
papers.f1_note: The abstract states no item count, so the rule's first source was unavailable.
papers.f2_quote: With this pipeline, we create LoCoMo, a dataset of 50 very long-term dialogues, each consisting of 300 turns and 9K tokens on avg., over up to 35 sessions. [Section 1]
papers.f4_quote: We report results from a single inference run for each model in our experiments [Appendix C.2]
papers.f6_caveat: Per-category accuracy on adversarial items, not a refusal rate over the benchmark. A stricter coder would record none.
papers.f9_quote: For each category, we calculate the F1 score for exact matches, following the normalization of both the predicted and the actual ground truth answers. [Section 4.1]
papers.propagation_finding: The count 50 appears in the Introduction and Table 5 but NOT in the abstract. This is a documented mechanism for downstream omission: A-MEM, which evaluates on LoCoMo, never states the conversation count.
flags: The string '50 conversations' occurs twice referring to apparently different sets: the human-verified benchmark set, and an unfiltered MiniGPT-5 training set in Section 5. Not reconciled by the paper.
Human baseline appears in Tables 2 and 4 with no stated annotator count or sample size.

papers.label: MemoryAgentBench
papers.title: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions
papers.f1_note: Neither abstract nor any results-table caption states a total. Column sum is 1800 or 2100 depending on an unresolved ambiguity in Table 1's Test-Time-Learning row.
papers.f2_rule_caveat: Rule 1 names conversations, sessions, or user histories; several sequences are documents or books. Mapping is by analogy and is recorded as such.
papers.f3_note: Not computable from a foregrounded F1. Conditional readings: 8.3 or 9.7.
papers.propagation_finding: The benchmark states its own non-independence explicitly and by design.
papers.key_quote: When curating datasets like EventQA and FactConsolidation, we deliberately design scenarios where multiple questions follow a single context. This allows us to probe the model's memory multiple times with one sequential injection.
flags: Items per sequence range from 1 to 200 across subsets; cluster sizes are severely unequal, which makes the equal-size design-effect approximation understate the true DEFF.

papers.label: MemBench
papers.title: MemBench: Towards More Comprehensive Evaluation on the Memory of LLM-based Agents
papers.f1_note: Largest foregrounded count is 39k questions (PS-FM, Table 2). Column sum of 53k is derived, not foregrounded.
papers.f2_quote: The dataset consists of two parts: (1) 500 graphs composed of user profiles and profiles of entities associated with users [Section 3.5]
papers.f2_rule_caveat: Rule 3 would select the same 500 graphs, since they are the generative seeds. Rule choice is not load-bearing here.
papers.f3_note: Full-dataset ratio. NOT computable for the reported experiments: the paper evaluates 1039 items and never states how many of the 500 graphs they come from.
papers.f7_note: Memory Efficiency concerns processing time costs, but that is a reported outcome, not an enforced parity constraint.
flags: The graph count behind the 1039 actually-evaluated items is not stated, which is the number a downstream user needs.

papers.label: MemoryArena
papers.title: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
papers.f1_quote: In total, we construct 766 representative multi-session interdependent agentic tasks. [Section 3]
papers.f1_discrepancy: Table 2's per-domain counts sum to 736, a 30-task gap the paper does not reconcile.
papers.f2_alternative: 5 is defensible if Math and Physics formal reasoning count as separate environments per Table 2.
papers.f6_caveat: Progress Score measures subtask completion but is a graded success metric, not a separately reported engagement or refusal rate. It does not distinguish an agent that attempted and failed from one that never attempted.
papers.self_disclosure: Subtasks within a task are stated to be interdependent by design, so subtask-level Progress Score is explicitly non-independent by the authors' own construction.
flags: Human annotators confirmed but annotator count not stated.

stratum_findings.uncertainty_guidance_note: Only LoCoMo discloses the absence, via 'a single inference run for each model'. The other three are silent.
stratum_findings.scoping: All counts describe the four benchmarks coded in this batch on 2026-07-24. They are not claims about benchmark practice in general.
